note: The entry follows Holmgren's 1910 original description (soldier and worker). The original is a library OCR text of a BHL scan (Zenodo/Plazi mirror); the German original description was read line by line; figures that the OCR scrambled beyond confirmation are not listed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 2.9—4 mm; head length 1.68—1.76 mm; head width 1.1—1.22 mm (5 specimens measured). Very similar to Eutermes major but slightly darker. Abdominal tergites covered with fine, rather dense hairs and with a transverse row of bristles before and behind; sternite hairs longer. Frontal outline almost straight, the elevation at the base of the nasus very small. Antennae 13-segmented: segment 3 longer than segment 2; segment 4 equal to segment 2; segment 5 longer than segment 4. Anterior margin of the pronotum not concave.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head red-brown (chestnut-brown) and rather glossy; fontanelle, transverse suture, middle and anterior part of the transverse band, region around the antennae, antennae, clypeus, labrum and base of the mandibles rusty yellow; the rest of the body red-yellow; anterior part of the head finely hairy; abdominal tergites with rather dense short hairs; the posterior margin of the tergites with or without bristle rows, the sternites always with marginal bristle rows. Head of the usual shape; fontanelle elongate-triangular; sagittal suture very fine and closed; transverse suture broad and open; clypeus shorter than half its width; mandibular condyles large. Antennae 14 or 15-segmented (with 14: segment 2 equal to segment 3; segment 4 far shorter than segment 3; segment 5 distinctly longer than segment 4; with 15: segment 3 less than half of segment 2; segment 4 slightly longer than segment 3; segment 5 equal to segment 4; segment 6 longer than segment 5). Anterior margin of the pronotum (very) distinctly concave. Worker body length 5 mm, head length 1.64 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality Tatarenda, Bolivia (collected by Nordenskiöld). Figure 32 of the original shows the soldier head in dorsal and lateral view.
